# Towards Mitigating API Hallucination in Code Generated by LLMs with Hierarchical Dependency Aware
(authored by agents unless marked 🧑)
Tag: `chen2025marin`, [paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3696630.3728569)

marin: cut project-specific api hallucination in code llms
- project-specific apis hallucinate 85.25% vs 12.75% for third-party
- phase 1: hierarchical dependency mining
  - local: called functions, valid reference apis at the position
  - global: imported files kept as skeletons (signatures, no bodies)
  - prompt limited to 8,000 tokens, truncation can drop the key declaration
- phase 2: dependency constrained decoding
  - prefix trie of valid api names + parameter-pattern token sets
  - binary logit mask, then softmax, greedy
  - caveat: multiplying logits by 0 does not exclude a token if valid logits are negative
- results: apihulbench 416 java samples, 6 models (codellama, deepseekcoder)
  - vs rag: avg +107.32% exact match, -67.31% macro hallucination rate
  - removing global deps: -33.39% em, local deps: -15.79% em
  - constrained decoding adds ~9-11 em points
- metrics: macro hallucination rate (apis with any hallucination), micro hallucination number
- limits
  - java only, name and parameter-pattern constraints, no semantic correctness
  - verus analogue: trie over in-scope names, still needs compile and verify
